## Purpose

`src/hooks/` is the layer between the thin `invoke()` wrappers in `src/lib` and the components. A hook here owns one query family: its cache key, its enablement guard, its staleness policy, and — for fan-outs — the shape of the per-project result rows. Components never talk to the backend directly — no component imports `invoke`, and that half holds everywhere. Owning the key is the direction of travel rather than the finished state: hooks own it for the families they cover, but 58 `queryKey:` literals still sit outside `src/hooks/` across 23 files. Keeping the key literals in one file per family is what lets the filesystem watcher invalidate by prefix instead of the pages polling. The hooks read as small and boring on purpose: the interesting decisions (why this staleTime, why no interval) live in comments right on the option they justify.

## Convention

Folder: apps/dashboard/src/hooks/** · Extension: .ts · Files of this role in this subproject: 20

- One file per hook family in this folder, named `use<Domain>.ts` (`.ts`, not `.tsx` — no JSX in this folder), exporting a named function of exactly the filename. Closely related companions live in the same file rather than a new one (`useIsMustardRepo` beside `useArtifactDrift`, `useWorkspaceSummarySingle` beside `useWorkspaceSummary`). No default exports.
- The hook imports its wrapper from `@/lib/dashboard`, `@/lib/projects`, `@/api/*` or a sibling `src/lib` module instead of reaching the backend itself — the subproject guard. `useTrace.ts:14` is the one file here that breaks it: it imports `invoke` directly and calls `dashboard_spec_trace` / `dashboard_session_trace` inside its own `queryFn`, because both commands return the same `TraceNode` and no `src/lib` wrapper was ever written for them. Do not copy that; add the wrapper first.
- Single-project query shape: `useQuery<T>({ queryKey: ["<kebab-literal>", repoPath, …leaves], queryFn: () => fetchX(repoPath as string), enabled: !!repoPath, staleTime: N_000 })`. Nullable inputs are typed `string | null`, gated by `enabled`, and cast `as string` inside the `queryFn` — that cast is the established idiom here, not a smell.
- Query keys are stable arrays with a kebab-case literal head and the project path / spec as leaves. Where a key would otherwise carry a value that moves every render, the hook keys on the stable input and derives the volatile value inside the `queryFn` (see the period-vs-window note in `useEconomySummary.ts`, plus its `stableScopeKey` helper that sorts array members so a reordered selection reuses the cache).
- Query-key ownership is an aspiration this folder has not finished collecting. 58 `queryKey:` literals live outside `src/hooks/`, over 23 files. Two groups of those are legitimate and stay: `src/lib/watcher.ts` re-spells 9 heads because prefix invalidation is its whole job, and the post-mutation `invalidateQueries` calls in `pages/Specs.tsx`, `pages/Settings.tsx`, `components/layout/Sidebar` and `components/layout/Topbar` name a key a hook already owns. The rest is the older shape — `pages/Specs.tsx`, `pages/Settings.tsx`, `pages/Economia.tsx`, `pages/Knowledge.tsx`, `pages/Activity.tsx`, `pages/Sessions.tsx`, `pages/ProjectDetail.tsx`, `features/specs/*`, `features/workspace/*`, `features/economy/ScopeBar` and `components/DoctorBadge` each declare a `useQuery` with an inline key. A new family gets a hook here; when you next touch one of those call sites, lifting its key into a hook is the improvement.
- Fan-out shape: `useQueries` over the list from `useProjectsStore((s) => s.projects)`, one query per `project.path` so cache identity follows the project, not the array index. The hook then returns either a 1:1 aligned array (`useProjectDetections`) or a `Record<path, Row>` (`useArtifactDrift`), each element `{ …identity, data: T | undefined, isLoading: q?.isLoading ?? false, error: q?.error }` — an unavailable report degrades to `undefined`, it does not break the row.
- Refresh is watcher-driven; a `refetchInterval` appears only where a panel is deliberately live and a comment says so (`useEconomySummary` at 30s). `retry: false` is used where the failure is structural (missing binary, non-Mustard repo).
- Mutations use `useMutation` + `useQueryClient` with pointwise `invalidateQueries` per affected key — no global sweeps — and report through `toast` from `sonner` in `onSuccess`/`onError` (`useSpecAction.ts`).
- Documentation is either a file header comment naming the spec/wave that introduced the hook (`useArtifactDrift`, `useEconomySummary`, `useProjectDetections`) or a JSDoc on the exported function for shorter files (`useFileContent`). Explicit return annotations (`UseQueryResult<T>`) appear on some hooks, not all.
- Not every hook is a query hook: `useTheme.ts` is plain `useState`/`useEffect`/`useCallback` with guarded `localStorage` access. Reach for TanStack only when there is a backend round-trip. Nor is every `use*` in the app in this folder: `useProjects` and `useActiveProjectName` live in `src/lib/dashboard.ts:387,411`, `useT`/`useTranslate` in `src/lib/i18n.ts`, and the zustand stores (`useStore`, `useProjectsStore`, `useCodeViewerStore`) in their own `src/lib` modules — this mold is about the query hooks in `src/hooks/`.

## How to apply

Create `src/hooks/use<Domain>.ts` next to its siblings. If the backend call does not exist yet, add the thin wrapper to `src/lib/dashboard.ts` (or a domain module under `src/lib`) first, keeping the `invoke` args in camelCase, then import it here. Choose the key head, register it with the watcher subscription if the data should tail live, and set `enabled` so the hook is safe to mount before a project is selected. For a per-project fan-out, copy the `useQueries` + aligned-rows shape and declare the row interface (`<Domain>Row`) in the same file above the hook. Components import the hook rather than re-implementing the query; the inline `useQuery` call sites listed in the Convention are the shape being retired, not a second sanctioned option.
